column1: # log-exempt.tsv (harbor#771) — every shell program in bin/ that does not yet log through
# bin/log-lib.sh, and why. Generated 2026-09-27 from lint LOG1's own census of the tree, so the
# list and the rule share one predicate. CONTRACTS/logging.md is the rule; LOG1 enforces this file:
#   - a row whose file changed since the base is refused: convert it, then drop the row;
#   - a row for a new file, or for one that already conforms, is refused;
#   - a shell program in bin/ outside the standard with no row is refused.
# So the wave-B and ratchet rows only shrink. A row whose file is gone is an advisory: it can exempt nothing.
# KIND  wave-B    an installer or box tool the install standard converts next, with install-lib
#       ratchet   outside the first scope; it converts the next time anyone edits it
#       protocol  PERMANENT: its stdout is a harness protocol (channel 3), so touching it never trips
#                 the ratchet; its why names the consumer ("Claude Code statusLine", "Claude Code
#                 <Event> hook"), LOG1 wants evidence the harness reads it, and a touched one keeps
#                 its stderr diagnostics in the line shape
